key_insight: A tool-calling LLM agent can translate everyday home-energy requests into appliance schedules that are often near-optimal, but only when every committed plan is checked by deterministic feasibility validation.
engineering_relevance: This work shows how LLMs can orchestrate residential energy assets under dynamic tariffs and solar forecasts, making them relevant for cost-aware, user-friendly home energy management and demand-side control.
method: ReAct-style agent converts natural-language preferences into schedules for multiple appliances
Uses Octopus Agile half-hourly prices, weather forecasts, PV generation estimates, and household demand data
Compares five LLM backends against a MILP benchmark across tariff, constraint, weather, and rolling-deployment tests
evidence_signal: Across a seven-day deployment, the agents captured 96.7-98.0% of the savings available between an off-peak timer and the MILP oracle and generally outperformed rule-based policies.
watch_item: LLM-generated schedules can be fabricated, infeasible, or inconsistent with the model’s explanation, so an independent validator is required before actuation.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
